messages.subject: Extracting Latent Response Variable Variances
parts:
Hello,

I'm modeling an ordinal SEM, and I wonder how can I extract the variances for the latent response variables on lavaan (in this case, represented by the vector x* with variance delta in the attached image)?

Thank you,
Deut

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Extracting Latent Response Variable Variances
parts:
On 02/17/2015 09:28 AM, Deuterium wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I'm modeling an ordinal SEM, and I wonder how can I extract the
> variances for the latent response variables on lavaan (in this case,

> represented by the vector /x*/ with variance /delta/ in the attached image)?

You can 'see' them in the summary() output, under the heading variances.
The values printed there are not free, (and hence have no standard error
under the default parameterization), but they are a function of other
model parameters.

If you need to 'extract' them, use the parameterEstimates() function,
which returns a standard data.frame.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Extracting Latent Response Variable Variances
parts:
On 02/20/2015 12:02 PM, Deuterium wrote:
> If they are not free, then based on what are they set to the values that
> I see (posted below)?

Look at the estimated model matrices,

inspect(fit, "est")

Now, the residuals are computed as:

DELTA^(-1/2) - diag( LAMBDA (I-B)^-1 PSI (I-B)^-T t(LAMBDA) )

where DELTA is the vector of scaling variables (usually set to 1, unless
you have multiple groups); LAMBDA are the factor loadings, PSI are the
factor variances/covariances, and B are the regression parameters.

Yves.
